name: loopboard-todo
description: Less prompting. No babysitting. More building. — the missing UI for Claude Code loops: your TODO.md as a live board your agents groom, build, and deliver from.

loopBoard.orchestrator.model.markdownDescription: The model the one Orchestrator loop session runs on (`claude --model`). It only routes the board: every groom, implementation and review is a subagent on the task's own model and effort, else the role default below. To point the alias at a specific model id (e.g. a 1M-context build), set that model's `loopBoard.models.<model>.modelId`. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.orchestrator.effort.markdownDescription: Reasoning effort the Orchestrator loop session is started with, passed as `claude --effort`. It sets the loop session itself only; subagents get their effort per spawn, from the task's `effort:` / `groomer-effort:`, else the role default (Claude Code 2.1.292+). `max` is not recommended: at max effort a session tends to over-split review work into many subagents and time out. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.orchestrator.groomConcurrency.markdownDescription: Cap on how many grooming subagents the Orchestrator may run in parallel during one pass (Rule 14 in `LOOP.md`). Eligible tasks over the cap are left in place, taken in index order top down, and picked up on a later pass: nothing is queued or dropped. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.defaultGroomerModel.markdownDescription: The model that grooms tasks and drafts with no `groomer:` field of their own. LoopBoard never picks a model for you: a spawn runs on the task's field, else this. The board's selects and new drafts use a change at once. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.defaultGroomerEffort.markdownDescription: Reasoning effort for grooming tasks and drafts with no `groomer-effort:` field, clamped into the groomer model's lowest and highest effort. The board's selects and new drafts use a change at once. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.defaultWorkerModel.markdownDescription: The model the implementer subagent runs on for tasks with no `model:` field of their own. LoopBoard never picks a model for you: a spawn runs on the task's field, else this. The board's selects and new drafts use a change at once. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.defaultWorkerEffort.markdownDescription: Reasoning effort for implementing tasks with no `effort:` field, clamped into the worker model's lowest and highest effort. A review runs at the same effort. The board's selects and new drafts use a change at once. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.defaultReviewerModel.markdownDescription: The model the review subagent runs on for tasks with no `reviewer:` field. `none`: no review subagent, the implementer's PR goes to Review directly. Any model (default `opus`): the review runs on it, at the task's worker effort (clamped into the reviewer model's range). A pass takes the task to Review with its PR still open; a fail is handed back to the implementer once, then parks the task in Feedback with the findings as questions. The loop never merges a PR. Replaces `loopBoard.delegateReview` (`true` became `opus`, `false` became `none`). The board's selects and new drafts use a change at once. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.models.opus.enabled.markdownDescription: **Opus.** Offer this task model in the board's selects, the settings page's role selects and the Orchestrator's bootstrap prompt. A model that is the Orchestrator's or a default groomer, worker or reviewer cannot be turned off. The board's selects and new drafts use a change at once. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.models.opus.modelId.markdownDescription: **Opus.** The model id the `opus` alias resolves to, for the Orchestrator session and every subagent spawned on `opus` (e.g. a pinned or 1M-context build such as `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`). Passed as the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` environment variable of the Orchestrator's terminal. Empty (default): the Claude Code CLI's own alias. Invalid ids are ignored. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.models.opus.minEffort.markdownDescription: **Opus.** The lowest effort any subagent on Opus runs at: a lower task or default effort is raised to it. A floor above `loopBoard.models.opus.maxEffort` is ignored (no clamping). Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.models.opus.maxEffort.markdownDescription: **Opus.** Default `xhigh`. The highest effort any subagent on Opus runs at: a higher task or default effort is lowered to it. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.permissionMode.markdownDescription: `--permission-mode` passed to the `claude` CLI when spawning a loop terminal. This setting is deliberately **user-scoped only** — a cloned repository must never be able to decide how much authority your agent runs with. Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.loopInterval.markdownDescription: Interval passed to `/loop`, in minutes: a whole number, bare or with `m` (e.g. `1m`, `5m`). Applies on the next loop start (▶) or restart (♻): a running loop keeps what it was spawned with.

loopBoard.contextLimit.percent.markdownDescription: Automatically restart the loop once its Claude session fills this percentage of its context window. `35` (default) restarts it at 35%; `0` turns the feature off, so the loop is never restarted for its context size; the usage bar under the running loop row still shows either way. The window is taken from the model that actually ran, as recorded in the session transcript (the 5-series models are 1,000,000 tokens natively; a `[1m]` suffix also means 1,000,000; anything unrecognised falls back to 200,000), so `35` on a 1M window is the 350k mark and on a 200k fallback window the 70k mark. A loop with a task In Progress or a live subagent is **never** interrupted: the restart waits for it to go idle.

enumDescriptions: Soft: send /clear to the terminal so the loop continues on a fresh conversation.
Hard: close the terminal and open a new one (default).
loopBoard.contextLimit.action.markdownDescription: What to do with a loop terminal when `loopBoard.contextLimit.percent` trips.

loopBoard.nudgeLoops.markdownDescription: When a board change gives the loop something to do (feedback on any card, a story whose questions are now FULLY answered, a task promoted to Backlog), paste a line naming that task into the Orchestrator's running loop terminal, so it acts on the change now instead of on its next scheduled pass. The text only seeds the REPL input, so it never interrupts work in flight, and it only ever supplements the loop's own board re-read. No running terminal: the nudge is held for its next start. Off disables the nudges entirely; loops keep working exactly as before.

loopBoard.idleStop.enabled.markdownDescription: Off (default): a loop runs until you stop it. On: stop a loop that has been idle for `loopBoard.idleStop.minutes` — idle meaning it owns no In Progress task and its session has no live subagent, the same busy test the context-limit restart waits on. A warning counts down the 30 seconds before the stop; its **Cancel** button keeps the loop running (restarts the idle clock), and with no click the stop goes ahead. The warning closes itself once the loop stops, turns busy or is stopped or restarted by hand. The stop is exactly the ■ button: the terminal closes and any scheduled start/restart/stop for that loop is cancelled. A busy loop is never stopped, and a loop that turns busy during the 30 seconds keeps running. Start it again with ▶.

loopBoard.idleStop.minutes.markdownDescription: Only applies while `loopBoard.idleStop.enabled` is on. How many minutes a loop must be idle before it is stopped; `60` (default). The warning appears 30 seconds before that mark, and the stop behaves exactly like the ■ button. An invalid value falls back to 60.

loopBoard.maxAttachmentSizeMB.markdownDescription: Maximum size (MB) for an image attached to a task (drag-drop, paste, or the picker). Attachments are staged under `.loopboard/cache/` and cleaned up on acceptance.

loopBoard.autoSyncTemplates.markdownDescription: Sync `.loopboard/` TODO.md and LOOP.md to the templates this extension ships, automatically, once when the window loads or the extension updates. It updates the extension-owned `loopboard:sync:` blocks and recreates missing files, and does a one-time legacy replacement of an unmarked LOOP.md (the old file is kept as `.loopboard/LOOP.md.bkp`) or an unmarked TODO.md intro. The `loopboard:custom` section and every task entry are never touched. Each auto-sync that writes shows a popup naming what changed. Off: nothing syncs by itself — use **Synchronise Templates** at the top of the LoopBoard settings page.

loopBoard.sidebarMarquee.markdownDescription: Scroll long In Progress task titles and subagent labels in the sidebar back and forth so the whole text passes by. Off (default) holds them still and truncates them with `…` instead; hover a row for the full text. The OS-level reduced-motion setting is honoured either way.

loopBoard.cardsStartCollapsed.markdownDescription: Start board cards collapsed in every phase tab (New, Backlog, In Progress, Feedback, Review). On (default) starts them collapsed; off starts them expanded. A tab you set with **Collapse all** / **Expand all** keeps its state until this setting changes; changing it resets every tab to the new value. Story sections stay folded either way.

enumDescriptions: No debug logging (default). Nothing is written and there is no overhead.
Key lifecycle events only: activation, promote/accept/demote gates, loop spawn/recycle/stop, same-field disk-wins conflicts.
Everything, including every field patch/save, attachment, template scaffold/heal/sync, config read, and webview message dispatch.
loopBoard.debug.markdownDescription: Opt-in verbose trace. With `info`/`verbose`, LoopBoard appends timestamped lines to `.loopboard/debug.log`. Field **values are logged verbatim** (no eliding), so keep `.loopboard/` in your `.gitignore` (recommended — LoopBoard does not add it) and the log is never committed. The log is tail-capped at 10 MB (oldest lines dropped); there is no separate command to open it.

loopBoard.showWhatsNew.markdownDescription: After LoopBoard updates, open a **What's New** tab once, on the first window load with a LoopBoard workspace. It names the version you updated to and links to its release notes on GitHub (the releases list when you skipped versions); LoopBoard fetches nothing. A first install or a downgrade opens nothing. The tab's **Don't show this again** tick turns this setting off.
